response: Yes, patient coaching can help reduce racial/ethnic disparities in cancer pain control. Studies have shown that targeted coaching interventions can improve pain management outcomes and reduce disparities in pain control among minority patients with cancer. By providing patients with the skills and knowledge to effectively communicate their pain and advocate for themselves, coaching can help address cultural and linguistic barriers that may contribute to disparities in care. Additionally, coaching can empower patients to take a more active role in their pain management, leading to better health outcomes and reduced disparities.
